content.text: No non-solicitation, no-hire, or employee-poaching restriction appears anywhere in the document, and § 12.3 affirmatively confirms the absence of any such commitment by Customer.

input.quote: Nothing restricts Customer from developing, acquiring, licensing, selling, or using any product or service, engaging any supplier, hiring any person who responds to general recruitment, or conducting business in any field or territory. Vendor acknowledges that Customer has made no exclusivity, non-compete, most-favoured-customer, minimum-volume, or no-hire commitment.
input.rationale: Searches for "solicit", "employ", "hire", "induce" and "recruit" across the full document return no non-solicitation, no-poach or no-hire covenant binding Customer (or either Party). This meets our preferred position of no non-solicit on Customer, so no fallback narrowing is needed. Section 12.3 goes further in our favour by expressly preserving Customer's freedom to hire anyone responding to general recruitment and recording that Customer has made no no-hire commitment; that language benefits us and is not flagged. Note for completeness that § 12.4 imposes a 24-month non-compete on Customer, but that is a competition/exclusivity restriction rather than a personnel non-solicit and is addressed under the separate restrictive-covenant rule, so it is not double-flagged here.
